_comment: English bodies for openai-agents-sdk (framework). Mechanism per C0-1..6. Official English quotes kept verbatim. layer_position/providers not rendered — not included.

axes.model_access:
**The official self-description is provider-agnostic.** The official access statement is one sentence:
the OpenAI two APIs are supported, and so are 100+ other LLMs.

**Official wording**: "It is provider-agnostic, supporting the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs, as well as **100+ other LLMs**."

The implementation path has two layers of evidence:

- The core dependency is `openai>=3.0.0`.
- There are two optional extras, both non-OpenAI paths.

The two extras are `litellm` (`openai-agents[litellm]`)
and `any-llm` (`openai-agents[any-llm]`, requires Python ≥3.11).

**The official `models` page gives the full access surface (verified).** The official docs dedicate
"Non-OpenAI models" and "Third-party adapters" sections.

Access points in those sections:

- **Built-in provider access points** can point at OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- Plus **Any-LLM / LiteLLM beta adapters**.

Official example of the built-in access point:

> `MultiProvider(openai_base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1")`

Official adapter example:

> `anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet`

The LiteLLM page's wording: one interface to 100+ models, and any AI model can be used.

**Official wording**: "allows you to use **100+ models** via a single interface ... use **any AI model** in the Agents SDK"

**Switching providers = change the `model`** (a string name / `LitellmModel(...)` / provider prefix).

⚠ But the official docs make **no "zero-change" quantitative promise**; per-vendor capability alignment needs testing.
axes.runtime:
**You run the process yourself — it is a library, not a service.**

All four run modes in the README are local code calls:

- `Runner.run_sync`
- `RealtimeRunner.run`
- `VoicePipeline.run`
- sandbox client

The only exception is **SandboxAgent's hosted sandbox client** —
the official docs mention a hosted sandbox is available.

⚠ But that depends on OpenAI-side container services; it is not "the whole agent hosted".
axes.local_files:
**Local-file capability explicitly exists, but not in the default agent.**

For scenarios that "need to inspect files, run commands, apply patches, or preserve workspace state across longer tasks"
the official docs provide **`SandboxAgent`** separately.

**Official wording**: SandboxAgent is preconfigured to work with a container to perform work over long time horizons

Its `default_manifest` can declare `GitRepo(repo=..., ref=...)`.

**Sandbox clients split by platform**:

- `UnixLocalSandboxClient` — macOS / Linux.
- Windows must use `DockerSandboxClient` (requires the `openai-agents[docker]` extra).
- Windows can also use the hosted sandbox client.

⚠ **A practical selection note: Windows users cannot use the local Unix sandbox path directly.**
axes.background:
**Self-hosted = stop it and it's gone.** The README has no hosted execution option
(Realtime is a long connection, but the process stays in your hands).

**Resuming after interruption has official support.** The Sessions section states
**Official wording**: "Automatic conversation history management across agent runs".

Optional backends include SQLite (SQLAlchemy dependency) and Redis (`openai-agents[redis]`).

SandboxAgent's default_manifest also targets
**Official wording**: "preserve workspace state across longer tasks".
axes.tools:
**The tool surface is the four kinds the official docs list**: functions, MCP, hosted tools,
and **agents as tools** (calling other agents as tools).

The latter two sit alongside handoffs as core delegation mechanisms.

**MCP is a core dependency, not optional.** See the dependency declaration:

- `mcp>=1.19.0,<3` is in `dependencies`.
- It is not in optional-dependencies — a first-class capability.

**Guardrails are configurable.** The official list includes "Configurable safety checks for
input and output validation", split into input and output directions.
axes.context:
**The official wording only has Sessions.**

**Official wording**: "Automatic conversation history management across agent runs"

Optional backends include Redis (`openai-agents[redis]`)
and SQLAlchemy (SQLAlchemy + asyncpg dependencies).

**Note the divergence from our claim.**

Sessions manages **conversation history**.

In our "state ≠ context" claim, measures like **spilling large tool outputs to disk**
are user-built in this SDK.

SandboxAgent's sandbox workspace can play that role, but the official docs do not market it as
a context-management layer.
axes.permissions:
**Built-in Guardrails (input + output two-way validation) + Human in the loop (tool-level approval).**

This is the **most complete permissions surface** we have seen built in so far. Two official lines:

**Official wording**: "Configurable safety checks for input and output validation"

**Official wording**: "Built-in mechanisms for involving humans across agent runs"

**Mechanism details verified** (official `guardrails` and `human_in_the_loop` chapters).
Guardrails come in three kinds:

- **input** — runs only on the first agent in the chain.
- **output** — runs only on the agent producing the final output.
- **tool** — wraps `FunctionTool`, validates before and after execution; can skip/replace/raise a tripwire.

The third kind's tripwire throws an exception and **aborts immediately**.

On the input side, `run_in_parallel=False` optionally intercepts before the agent starts.

**Tool-level approval**: `needs_approval=True|callable` works on
`function_tool`, `ShellTool`, `ApplyPatchTool`, `Agent.as_tool`.

MCP servers use `require_approval`.

Approvals pause via run-wide `interruptions`; `RunState` is serializable/resumable.
When arguments cannot be safely parsed it **fails closed**; `always_approve` can pin a decision.

⚠ **State the boundary**: the official docs have **no** built-in file/network sandbox.

guardrails are **user-programmable validation hooks**; the real sandbox boundary is left to the host machine or
the SandboxAgent container, not the guardrail layer.

(guardrails, human_in_the_loop, and Sandbox agents pages checked.)

This contrasts sharply with Deep Agents' **"trust the LLM, boundary responsibility is yours"**.
axes.fit:
**Fits**:

- You want a "thin harness" and choose everything beyond the agent loop primitives yourself.
- You need guardrails and human-in-the-loop built in.
- You need first-class MCP support and your team is on Python.

**Does not fit**:

- You want a batteries-included long-task workspace.
- You are in the TypeScript ecosystem (use openai-agents-js).

Both "does not fit" items have alternative routes: for the long-task workspace use Deep Agents,
or take this SDK's SandboxAgent route.

sections.provider-agnostic 是官方写在首段的:
The official first paragraph puts this up front:

> The OpenAI Agents SDK is a lightweight yet powerful framework for building multi-agent workflows.

> It is **provider-agnostic**, supporting the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs, as well as **100+ other LLMs**.

**This is our first decision point.** The code-level evidence agrees:

- Core dependency `openai>=3.0.0`.
- Two optional extras `litellm` and `any-llm`, as non-OpenAI paths.

⚠ But state the boundary: **"100+" is an official claim; we have not measured the capability alignment of specific providers.**

Tool calling, structured output, and multimodal support vary a lot across vendors.
sections.与 Deep Agents 的对照：本站最该给用户看的一张表:
Both sit in the Python agent-harness tier, with completely opposite styles:

| Dimension | **OpenAI Agents SDK** | **Deep Agents** |
|---|---|---|
| Style | primitives-only, thin | batteries-included, thick |
| filesystem | not preset (wire your own, or use SandboxAgent) | **core selling point**, pluggable backends |
| subagents | agents as tools / handoffs (build them yourself) | **preset** sub-agents |
| context management | only Sessions (conversation history) | summarize + **disk spill** + cross-session memory |
| permissions | **built-in guardrails + human-in-the-loop** | officially "trust the LLM"; boundaries are yours |
| run form | you run it (local/container/Redis) | you run it |

**Selection rule**: want security built in → the former; want features built in → the latter.
sections.SandboxAgent：本地文件能力的官方答案，但有个 Windows 坑:
A plain `Agent` carries no local workspace. For this the official docs provide **`SandboxAgent`**:

> Use a `SandboxAgent` when the agent needs to inspect files, run commands, apply patches, or **preserve workspace state across longer tasks**.

Its `default_manifest` can declare repositories to check out:

```python
agent = SandboxAgent(
    name="Workspace Assistant",
    default_manifest=Manifest(
        entries={"repo": GitRepo(repo="openai/openai-agents-python", ref="main")}
    ),
)
```

⚠ **Platform differences are selection-critical**:

| Client | Supported platforms | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `UnixLocalSandboxClient` | macOS / Linux | the README example uses it |
| `DockerSandboxClient` | Windows etc. | requires the `openai-agents[docker]` extra |
| hosted sandbox client | depends on OpenAI-side services | officially mentioned as available |

**Windows users cannot take the local Unix sandbox path directly.**
sections.权限面：目前本站见到的最完整内建方案:
| Officially provided | Section |
|---|---|
| **Guardrails** (input + output two-way validation) | "Configurable safety checks for input and output validation" |
| **Human in the loop** (involving humans across runs) | "Built-in mechanisms for involving humans across agent runs" |

**Contrast with Deep Agents' official statement** (verbatim):

> Deep Agents follows a "trust the LLM" model... Enforce boundaries at the tool/sandbox level, not by expecting the model to self-police.

**These two sentences are the two answers to our "who owns permissions" question** — and a real selection criterion.

> **Do you want built-in input/output validation, or do you want to draw the sandbox boundary yourself?**

**Mechanism verified (see axes.permissions)**:

- guardrails split into input / output / tool, with a tripwire abort on hit.
- Tool-level approval `needs_approval` covers function_tool / ShellTool / ApplyPatchTool / MCP.

⚠ **Boundary: no built-in file/network sandbox officially.**

A guardrail is a user-programmable validation hook. The real sandbox boundary is left to the host machine or the SandboxAgent container.
sections.「状态 ≠ 上下文」在这两个 SDK 里的不同答案:
| | OpenAI Agents SDK | Deep Agents |
|---|---|---|
| Conversation history | Sessions (Redis / SQLAlchemy backends) | persistent memory (pluggable state and store) |
| Long context | **no official context-management layer** | summarize long threads |
| Large-output disk spill | **no official claim** (SandboxAgent's workspace can serve the role) | **offload tool outputs to disk** |

When we argue "persistence ≠ compression", **Deep Agents is the side with official disk-spill mechanisms**.

⚠ But note: SandboxAgent's workspace preservation (preserve workspace state)
is itself a form of persistence.

The official docs just don't classify it as context management.

**This is our judgment, not an official statement — marked as inference.**
sections.MCP 是一等能力，不是可选插件:
In `pyproject.toml`, `mcp>=1.19.0,<3` sits in **`dependencies`**, not `optional-dependencies`.

The official README lists MCP alongside functions and hosted tools as tool types.

**In this SDK, connecting an MCP server requires installing nothing extra.**

The README explicitly points to `openai/openai-agents-js` (rolling verification 2026-10-23: MIT, 3,935★, active).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/framework/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/framework/_protocol.md).

**Suggested runs** (tailored to this SDK within the harness section's five dimensions):

| # | What to test | Why it is worth testing |
|:--:|---|---|
| 1 | How many files and lines for a minimal hello agent | officially called lightweight — verify just how "thin" |
| 2 | Can Guardrails block an over-reach like "read a file" | officially positioned as input/output validation, not file-access permission |
| 3 | Minimal usable path of SandboxAgent on **Windows** | the official example is Unix; Windows needs Docker |
| 4 | How much changes when switching to litellm / any-llm with a local model | officially provider-agnostic — verify the real diff size |
| 5 | After killing the process, does Sessions restore state completely | our biggest "reliable long-running" concern |
unknowns:
- A capability-alignment matrix across the 100+ providers

- Concurrent-write semantics of Sessions backends across multi-process/multi-machine
- The real dependency footprint and upgrade conflicts of the litellm / any-llm extras
related: **The pair most worth contrasting on our site**: Deep Agents is batteries-included (filesystem + subagents + context management); this SDK is primitives-only. Two branches of the same decision tree.
Also in the "coding-base" tier, also from a model vendor. The OpenAI side goes primitives-only + built-in guardrails; the Anthropic side's home turf is Claude Code.
LangGraph is a graph runtime; the OpenAI Agents SDK is an agent harness — composable (use the graph as a tool/subagent), but at different layers.
